messages.text:
"Mobile landscape top-down firefighter rescue game called Mr. Rescue: Extinguish Protocol. Pixel art style inspired by classic Mr. Rescue (red helmet firefighter, yellow suit, burning building rooms with furniture and windows).

Controls: Dual virtual joysticks that appear on touch. Left side of screen = movement joystick. Right side = aim and fire joystick. Bottom button to switch extinguisher type between Water, Foam, Cryo, and CO2. Fullscreen landscape.

Core gameplay: Rescue civilians by picking them up or escorting them to exits/windows. Heat rises near fire (coolant pickups reduce it; full heat = death). Each extinguisher has limited ammo. Fire spreads over time. Score based on civilians saved.

Four moving enemy types that only die to the matching extinguisher (wrong type does nothing or makes it worse): Water vs Charcoal/Ember, Foam vs Magma/Oil, Cryo vs Frostfire, CO2 vs Gas Phantom. Enemies patrol and chase. Puzzle elements: path-blocking fires that need the correct extinguisher, simple environmental interactions, and mixed enemy rooms that force switching.

Challenging and tense. Multiple rooms, progress by rescuing civilians then reaching the exit. Show heat bar, current extinguisher + ammo, score, and civilians remaining. End of floor requires most civilians rescued.

---

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable mobile-landscape top-down pixel-art firefighter rescue game, “Mr. Rescue: Extinguish Protocol.”

## Requirements
- Dual virtual joysticks on touch: left moves, right aims and fires; extinguisher switch button; fullscreen landscape.
- Rescue civilians, manage rising heat and coolant pickups, limited extinguisher ammo, spreading fires, matching-only enemy weaknesses, multiple rooms, environmental interactions, score, and a minimum rescue count to clear a floor.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Implemented the game as a standalone HTML canvas app with embedded CSS and JavaScript.
- Assumed one floor with three sectors, six civilians, and four civilians required to win.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added a playable game in `index.html` with pixel-art rendering, enemies, fires, four extinguishers, pickups, civilian rescue, HUD, title/pause/win/lose screens, keyboard/mouse/touch controls, and fullscreen support.
- JavaScript syntax checked successfully.
- Launched the game in Playwright and saved/read a JPEG screenshot at `screenshots/latest.jpg`.

### Active
- Review gameplay behavior and address any issues discovered during testing.

### Blocked
- Browser showed one resource error for missing `favicon.ico` (404); game itself loaded.

## Next Move
1. Inspect game behavior in-browser and verify controls, rescue flow, enemies, and floor completion.
2. Consider adding a favicon or suppressing the 404, then rerun the browser check.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Complete game implementation.
- `screenshots/latest.jpg`: Most recent browser screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Browser console reported only `Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (File not found) @ http://localhost:3002/favicon.ico:0`.
